overall: Atlanta is currently at 78.8°F as of 10:50 ET and warming briskly at +3.6°F/hr under mostly sunny skies with scattered clouds at 38% coverage. The day is tracking slightly behind an 83°F peak but still has roughly 3-4 hours of heating before the expected afternoon maximum near 14-15h ET. Conditions are drier than overnight (dewpoint 66.2°F vs earlier 71°F range) and a stiff northwest wind at 17 mph is adding a modest cooling offset against solar heating.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show exceptionally tight agreement: ECMWF 81.4°F, HRRR 82.2°F, and NBM 82.6°F all cluster within a 1.2°F range, and the NWS text forecast of 'near 83°F' aligns squarely with that consensus. The active flood warnings are confined to the Satilla River basin in far southeast Georgia (Pierce, Ware, and Brantley counties) and have no bearing on Atlanta's temperature today.
max_temp_prediction: The META model (most reliable fusion of daily and intraday signals) concentrates ~55% of probability in the 82–85°F range, with the 82-83°F and 84-85°F buckets tied at 27.7% each. Given the tight NWP model consensus around 81-83°F, the NWS 83°F forecast, the current warming trajectory still ~4°F shy of the target with 3+ hours of peak solar heating remaining, and slightly elevated dewpoints that will temper afternoon warming somewhat, confidence is moderate-to-high that the high lands near 83°F. A modest overshoot into the mid-80s is possible if the current +3.6°F/hr warming rate sustains, but the northwest wind gusts are likely to cap gains.
